headline: A 2018 executive order lets the US Marshals Service fill certain jobs without the usual competitive federal hiring exams.
what_it_does: Most federal jobs are filled through competitive examining, a standard process for ranking and choosing applicants. Based on its title, this order creates an exception to those rules for some positions in the US Marshals Service, part of the Department of Justice. The title does not say which positions are covered or what hiring process replaces the usual one.

who_it_affects.group: People applying for certain US Marshals Service jobs
who_it_affects.how: They may be hired through a different process than the standard competitive federal hiring exams.

who_it_affects.group: US Marshals Service and Department of Justice hiring officials
who_it_affects.how: They gain an exception from the usual competitive hiring rules when filling the covered positions.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed July 10, 2018; the title does not give a separate start date.
